classification.difficultyReason: Connect the right-angle condition to a squared-distance equation, then complete squares and interpret the locus. Identifying excluded endpoints and establishing the converse require reasoning beyond the supplied equation.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the coordinates of $P$ satisfy
$$x^2-4x+y^2-12y+30=0.$$

answer.worked:
Since $\angle APB=90^\circ$, Pythagoras gives $PA^2+PB^2=AB^2$.

$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=(3-1)^2+(9-3)^2\\AB^2&=40\end{align*}$$

Using the distance formula,
$$\begin{align*}(x-1)^2+(y-3)^2+(x-3)^2+(y-9)^2&=40\\2x^2-8x+2y^2-24y+100&=40\\2x^2-8x+2y^2-24y+60&=0\\x^2-4x+y^2-12y+30&=0\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, sketch the set of all possible positions of $P$.

answer.short:
The circle $(x-2)^2+(y-6)^2=10$, with centre $(2,6)$ and radius $\sqrt{10}$, excluding $A(1,3)$ and $B(3,9)$.

Complete the square. Show open markers at $A$ and $B$, where $\angle APB$ is undefined.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}x^2-4x+y^2-12y+30&=0\\(x-2)^2-4+(y-6)^2-36+30&=0\\(x-2)^2+(y-6)^2&=10\end{align*}$$

The centre is $(2,6)$ and the radius is $\sqrt{10}$. The midpoint of $AB$ is $(2,6)$ and $AB=2\sqrt{10}$, so $AB$ is a diameter.

Exclude $A(1,3)$ and $B(3,9)$ because the angle is undefined when $P$ equals either endpoint.

Conversely, any other point on this circle satisfies $PA^2+PB^2=AB^2$ by reversing the algebra in part (a). By the converse of Pythagoras, $\angle APB=90^\circ$. Thus every remaining point on the circle belongs to the locus.
